common_name: Daylily 'Winsome Lady' (Fragrant Blush-Pink Lenington Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Winsome Lady is a dormant-foliage diploid registered in 1964 that earned the AHS Lenington All-American Award in 1974 for its wide-area garden reliability.

directions: Winsome Lady opens blush-pink self blooms about five and a half inches across with a deep green throat, carried on scapes around two feet tall during the early season. The flowers are notably fragrant and the plant reblooms reliably, a combination that helped it earn the Lenington All-American Award for consistent performance across diverse US climates. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep bloom counts high.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jest is a dormant-foliage diploid registered in 1963 that won the AHS Lenington All-American Award in 1975.

directions: Jest bears small, clear lemon-yellow self flowers only about three inches across with a green throat, opening on scapes roughly twenty inches tall with an extended, nocturnal habit that keeps blooms open into the evening. Flowering runs midseason to late, and the compact plant's dependable performance over many regions earned it the Lenington All-American Award. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and divide clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; White Formal is a semi-evergreen diploid registered in 1965 by hybridizer George Lenington that won the AHS Lenington All-American Award in 1977.

directions: White Formal produces near-white self blooms about five and a half inches wide with a contrasting green throat, held on tall scapes around thirty inches high during midseason. Its semi-evergreen foliage and dependable flowering across widely varying regional climates earned it the Lenington All-American Award, named for its own hybridizer George Lenington. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, and divide crowded clumps in spring every few years to sustain bloom production.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Midnight Magic is an evergreen tetraploid registered by John Kinnebrew in 1979, bred from Ed Murray crossed with Kilimanjaro, that won the AHS Lenington All-American Award in 2002.

directions: Midnight Magic opens velvety black-red self blooms about five and a half inches across with a green throat, carried on well-branched scapes around twenty-eight inches tall from early to midseason. This evergreen tetraploid was bred from 'Ed Murray' crossed with 'Kilimanjaro' and went on to win the Lenington All-American Award for its outstanding bud count and reliable performance across diverse climates. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
